module_summary: These are ee_core's interface headers and link scripts. coreconfig.h defines EECoreConfig_t, the block the launcher (src/platform/system.cpp sysLaunchLoaderElf) fills inside the embedded eecore.elf: IP strings, exit path, cheat and RA pointers, in-game-menu fields. modules.h numbers the IRX blobs the launcher packs and modmgr.c looks up. The other headers declare the IGR, pad-hook (with the libpad/libpad2 signature tables in padpatterns.h), GSM, IGS, cheat engine, in-game menu (igrmenu/igrmbox/igrcheats/igrmfont), freeze-report and RA interfaces. ee_core/linkfile places the core at 0x84000 with the stack in whatever ram84 leaves below 0x97000 (assert >= 3 KB). igrovl/ is the RA editions' in-game-menu overlay linked at 0xCC000-0xD0000 and called through igrovl_api_t. ee_core/Makefile is the legacy, unused make build and debug_colors_doc.sh a doc generator.

reusable_helpers.name: igrCheatsBuild
reusable_helpers.what: builds the engine's [count][addr,val pairs] code set from the ticked cheat rows, whole cheats in file order while they fit 250 pairs

reusable_helpers.name: igrCheatsFit
reusable_helpers.what: checks whether the ticked rows plus one more row fit one code set

reusable_helpers.name: eeResetPayloadLength
reusable_helpers.what: bounds the payload length of an intercepted SifResetIop packet against packet and command capacity

reusable_helpers.name: strlen
reusable_helpers.what: freestanding strlen for the libc-free overlay

findings.title: Unchecked eth_linkmode from conf_network.cfg makes ee_core index SmapLinkModeArgs[mode-1] out of bounds; ps2_ip can overrun g_ps2_ip[16]
findings.problem: settingsio.cpp:1924 reads eth_linkmode with configGetInt and no check; system.cpp:1561 truncates it into the u8 g_ps2_ETHOpMode. set_ipconfig (util.c:96-99, run at every game start from main.c:154) tests only != AUTO and then reads SmapLinkModeArgs[mode-1], a 4-entry local array, so eth_linkmode=5..255 (or -1) reads a stack word as a char* and strncpy copies 6 bytes from it: garbage SMAP args or an address error at game start. The menu treats these values as AUTO (netsupport.cpp:408-423). Second path: in UDPBD/UDPFS modes system.cpp:1580 sprintf's unchecked %d ps2_ip values (sscanf at settingsio.cpp:1950) into g_ps2_ip[16]; a field over 3 digits leaves it unterminated, strlen at util.c:85 then spans the netmask, and with a non-auto link mode g_ipconfig[64] overflows by up to ~15 bytes.
findings.fix: In util.c:96 also require g_ps2_ETHOpMode < ETH_OP_MODE_COUNT (the unused enum end at ee_core.h:51), so out-of-range values act as AUTO like the menu. At system.cpp:1580 print the four values as (u8) with %u, as line 1577 already does, or use snprintf with sizeof(config->g_ps2_ip).
findings.justification: Both changes stay on existing lines (one extra condition, one format change). They close an out-of-bounds read that can crash every launch and a .bss overrun, both caused by one bad config value.
findings.benefit: Removes an out-of-bounds stack read (wild-pointer strncpy) at ee_core init and a g_ipconfig overrun of up to ~15 bytes (INFERRED from 16+16+16+9+6 byte layout); 0 lines net
findings.evidence: Read util.c:71-102 (SmapLinkModeArgs[4] local, index g_ps2_ETHOpMode-1, guard only != ETH_OP_MODE_AUTO); main.c:154 calls set_ipconfig unconditionally; settingsio.cpp:1921-1956 (configGetInt eth_linkmode, sscanf %d ps2_ip, no range checks); system.cpp:1561 (u8 copy), 1577-1582 (%d sprintf into char[16] only for sysModeIsNetBlock); netsupport.cpp:408-423 default -> AUTO. grep ETH_OP_MODE_COUNT: only definitions at ee_core.h:51 and include/opl.h:115. GUI path (guisettings.cpp:985 diaGetInt) is an enum list, so the trigger is a hand-edited or corrupted conf_network.cfg. INFERRED: what the out-of-range stack word holds, hence crash vs garbage args.

findings.title: EE_RESET_SUFFIX_BYTES is 7 but ResetIopSpecial writes 8 bytes after the payload (latent one-byte stack overflow of command[])
findings.problem: ResetIopSpecial accepts arglen up to sizeof(command) - 7, then writes the NUL at command[arglen] and _strcpy's "host0:" with its terminator (util.c:24-27 copies strlen+1) to command[arglen+1..arglen+7], so arglen = sizeof(command)-7 writes command[sizeof(command)], one past the stack array. eeResetPayloadLength repeats the same 7 for commandCapacity, and the test pins it ((19,80,16) == 9 means 9+8 = 17 bytes into 16). Not reachable today: the only caller passes packetCapacity = sizeof(SifCmdResetData_t.arg), which caps the payload at 70 for an 80-byte arg (INFERRED SDK size), below the 73 the guard allows.
findings.fix: Set EE_RESET_SUFFIX_BYTES to 8 and fix its comment (NUL, "host0:" and its NUL). Change the test's (19,80,16) case to expect -1 and (20,80,16) stays -1.
findings.benefit: Corrects a latent off-by-one in the reset-command bound; no size change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read reset_arg_bounds.h:1-21, iopmgr.c:74-96 (char command[RESET_ARG_MAX + 1]; guard arglen > sizeof(command) - EE_RESET_SUFFIX_BYTES; command[arglen]=0; _strcpy(&command[arglen+1], "host0:")), util.c:24-27 (_strcpy copies the terminator), iopmgr.c:436-439 (only caller with args). grep eeResetPayloadLength/EE_RESET_*: iopmgr.c and test_reset_arg_bounds.py only. Unreachability INFERRED from RESET_ARG_MAX 79 and arg[RESET_ARG_MAX + 1] as stubbed in test_reset_failure_lifecycle.py:31-32; the real SDK header was not read.
